title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park: Protect Yourself from Volcanic Tephra
summary: Volcanic ash, rock and glassy strands (tephra) is present at Kīlauea summit and can irritate your skin, eyes and respiratory system. For your safety, do not handle it. Eye protection, long sleeves, long pants, a hat, closed-toe shoes and a dust mask are recommended.

title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park: Upper Kahuku Road Closed Beyond Boot Decontamination Station
summary: Upper Kahuku Road remains closed beyond the boot decontamination station due to storm damage. The Visitor Contact Station and most trails in the Kahuku Unit are now open following Hurricane Lala. Kahuku Road above the Lower Palm Trailhead is deeply rutted by the recent heavy rains. A 4WD is recommended to access areas above the Lower Palm Trailhead.

title: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park: Annual and lifetime passes not available for purchase
summary: Annual and lifetime passes are not currently available for purchase at Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park. As an alternative, you can purchase an annual pass online.
place: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park

title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park: Sulphur Banks Bridge Closed; Boardwalk is Open
summary: The Sulphur Banks Bridge is damaged and closed until further notice. The Haʻakulamanu area, boardwalk and Sulphur Banks Trail are open and accessible from the west side near Steam Vents.

title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park: Kīpukapuaulu Trail Closed Due to Hazardous Trees and Hanging Limbs
summary: Kīpukapuaulu Trail remains closed due to numerous hazardous trees and hanging limbs resulting from several recent storms. Managers are developing a plan and will reopen the trail when it is safe.

title: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park: Section of Trail Closed
summary: Please note that the 1871 Trail beyond Alahaka Ramp is closed.

title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park: Kīlauea eruption
summary: Volcanic eruptions can be hazardous. Stay out of closed areas and monitor air quality. Eruptions can last a few hours and are often separated by pauses lasting several weeks.

title: Ala Kahakai National Historic Trail
summary: Established in 2000 to preserve, protect and interpret traditional Native Hawaiian culture and natural resources, Ala Kahakai National Historic Trail is a 175-mile corridor encompassing a network of culturally and historically significant trails. This "trail by the sea" traverses wahi pana (storied landscapes), ancient Hawaiian sites and over 200 ahupuaʻa (traditional land divisions).

title: Hakalau Forest National Wildlife Refuge
summary: Hakalau Forest NWR contains some of the finest remaining stands of native montane rain forest in Hawai‘i. The slopes below 4,000 feet receive very high rainfall - 250 inches annually. Bogs, fern patches, and scrubby forest dominate this area which is dissected by numerous deep gulches. title: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park
summary: Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park protects some of the most unique geological, biological, and cherished cultural landscapes in the world. Extending from sea level to 13,680 feet, the park encompasses the summits of two of the world's most active volcanoes - Kīlauea and Mauna Loa - and is a designated International Biosphere Reserve and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau National Historical Park
summary: Imagine you had just broken the sacred laws, the kapu, and the only punishment was death. Your only chance of survival is to elude your pursuers and reach the Puʻuhonua, a place of refuge. The Puʻuhonua protected the kapu breaker, defeated warriors, as well as civilians during the time of battle. No physical harm could come to those who reached the boundaries of the Puʻuhonua.
